questions.subject: WEB_DEVELOPMENT
questions.topic: Heading levels are structure rather than size
questions.learningObjective: Recognize that heading level is not font size
questions.stem: During review, someone argues h6 must be the smallest text on the page.

options.text: h6 is always the smallest text by rule
Browsers forbid styling h6 larger
Heading level is structure, size is CSS
Only h1 through h3 can be styled

questions.explanation: Heading level encodes structure, not size. CSS can make h6 any size, and browsers do not enforce ordering.

questions.subject: WEB_DEVELOPMENT
questions.topic: What a form actually submits
questions.learningObjective: Explain submission of radio button groups
questions.stem: A ticket asks why a radio button group submits only one value even when multiple are checked via scripting.

answer.exemplar: Radio buttons sharing a name form a mutually exclusive group, so only the selected value is submitted, and scripting cannot make multiple values submit under one name.

questions.explanation: Radio buttons with the same name are mutually exclusive, so only one value submits. Scripting does not change that grouping rule.

questions.topic: Display decides block or inline, not the tag name
questions.learningObjective: Explain display:contents removes box
questions.stem: A ticket asks what display:contents does to an element's own box in the layout.

answer.exemplar: display:contents removes the element's own box so its children participate in the parent layout, while the element remains in the DOM tree.

questions.explanation: The element's box is removed from layout, but children still render and the node stays in the DOM. It does not delete the element.
